reviewAdvisory: The 30 litres/100km consumption rate and 0.84 kg/l density are assumed baselines not present in the supplied figures, so the per-kilometre and per-tonne savings are not derivable from the NDRC announcement alone.

The 10-working-day window and the international crude basket linkage are asserted as mechanism detail the supplied evidence does not contain, and the draft presents them as established fact rather than inference.
The provincial ceiling-price process and quality differentials are described as fact without a cited provincial notice or regulation in the figures, so the reader cannot verify the mechanism.

The confidence section labels the consumption and density as assumptions, but the body presents the resulting savings as arithmetic facts and the table as estimates only in a trailing sentence, so the confidence section contradicts the body's framing.
The 0.72 kg/l gasoline density is a new assumed baseline not in the figures and not disclosed as an assumption in the FAQ, so the per-litre figures are not derivable from the supplied evidence.

The declared information gain is a custom calculation, but the calculation rests on assumed consumption and density values the figures do not contain, so the gain is not supported by the supplied evidence.
